title: Purrfect Pal: Care Shift
premise: A cozy real-time virtual pet game where you manage a cat's needs during a hectic care shift by earning tips, buying food, playing, and scheduling naps before trust runs out.
interaction_model: Single-screen touch/click play using HUD action buttons, direct tapping on the pet for affection, and tapping spawned coin pickups on the canvas to collect money.
objective: Keep the cat's hunger, fun, energy, and trust/happiness stable for as long as possible while using work shifts and a small food economy to prevent a runaway decline into game over.
progression: Run-based survival progression with continuous stat pressure, work cooldown management, inventory upkeep, and restart-based replay rather than levels or story chapters.
theme: Cute pet caregiving with a magical neon lounge presentation and a light workplace 'care shift' framing.
mood: Cozy, charming, affectionate, and mildly hectic under soft real-time pressure.
likely_audience: players who enjoy cute maintenance loops
confidence_notes: High confidence that the primary genre is virtual pet / pet simulator because the central loop revolves around maintaining multiple pet needs in real time.
High confidence in the resource-management layer because money, food stock, cooldowns, and action tradeoffs are explicit in code.
Moderate confidence on intended difficulty scaling because there are no formal stages; tension comes from decay interactions instead of authored progression.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first single-screen virtual pet game called "Purrfect Pal: Care Shift" where the player cares for a cute animated cat in real time on a full-screen canvas with a cozy purple glassmorphism HUD. The pet should have four constantly changing need bars—food, fun, energy, and trust—and the run should end if trust drops to zero. The main loop is a balancing act: press a Shift button to spawn several bouncing coin pickups on the playfield, tap those coins to collect tip money, spend money in a small shop modal to buy fish food into inventory, use stored food to feed the cat, press Play to raise fun at the cost of energy, toggle Sleep/Wake to let energy recover over time while some other needs still decay, and tap directly on the cat to give affection that slightly restores trust. While awake, needs should decay continuously, and trust should decay faster when hunger, fun, or energy are low so neglect snowballs into failure. The cat should visibly react through cute animations, blinking, sleeping poses with floating Zzz text, playful effects, warning emojis when needs are low, and floating heart or sparkle particles for positive interactions. Include compact touch-friendly buttons, progress bars, toast messages, lightweight haptics/SFX, a looping background track, positive and negative animated feedback badges, a work cooldown overlay, a shop for buying and serving food, and a game-over overlay that says the pal wandered off after losing trust. The overall tone should feel adorable, polished, and slightly hectic, like a Tamagotchi-style pet sim mixed with a tiny resource-management survival loop built for short repeatable sessions.
